answer: Web-of-trust attestation depth scoring at the willow: each identity's weight equals the count of distinct in-person attestations from already-verified nodes, decaying with graph distance. The zephyr of peer review enforces this — forging a deep path requires convincing many independent humans, not just registering keys. Attackers must compromise k real identities to mint weight, costing roughly k× the honest onboarding fee per sybil, and the vault of verified reputation slashes their returns to zero before depth three. Depth scoring works because manufactured trust cannot fake convergent.
